label: rare transition a1 -> S2 (D2)
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only when the reached-state input is S2 (never at D1/GO, never on S1). 94% of activation mass is on D2 steps where the agent chose a1 and landed in S2, i.e. the rare transition a1->S2; the remaining 6% are weak activations on common a2->S2 steps. All variables are observed at D2 (state and last-action inputs). Magnitude is highest when the previous reward was 0 (prev_reward==0 restriction covers 82% of the top activation quartile but only 12% of the bottom), e.g. strings of unrewarded a1 rare trials reach the max; it is weaker after a rewarded trial. About 22% of rare a1->S2 steps stay below threshold, mostly after rewarded common a1 trials. Adding history conditions (prev reward/transition, policy logit) did not improve F1 over the simple input conjunction.

issues: All the main factual claims hold on dev. Phase D1 and GO have 0 active steps each, so all activation mass is on D2. in_state==1 has 0 active steps. in_action==1 carries 0.939 of the mass and in_action==2 carries 0.061. in_rew==1 never fires.
The scores reproduce. Dev: P 0.779, R 0.879, F1 0.826, mass recall 0.939. Test: P 0.774, R 0.854, F1 0.812, mass recall 0.926.
The magnitude claim checks out. B & prev_reward==0 covers 0.82 of the top quartile and 0.12 of the bottom quartile. Excluding steps after a rewarded common a1 trial gives F1 0.58, as reported.

The explanation leaves out one systematic class of false positives. When the previous trial was rare and rewarded, rare a1->S2 steps are mostly silent. B & prev_reward==1 & prev_common==0 has precision 0.21 (about 2520 dev steps), versus 0.75 after a rewarded common trial. This holds for both previous actions (0.21 after a1, 0.22 after a2). Excluding this class raises F1 a little: dev 0.838, test 0.823.

The 6% of mass on common a2->S2 is not scattered. It concentrates on trials where the previous trial was an unrewarded a1. D2 & S2 & a2 & prev_action==1 & prev_reward==0 has precision 0.45, against about 0.03 for a2->S2 overall. Activations there are weak (bottom quartiles).

The claim that misses are 'mostly ones that follow a rewarded common a1 trial' is roughly right: about 56% of the false positives follow one. But rare-rewarded history is a much stronger suppressor per step (79% inactive) and is not mentioned.
These are small refinements, under 0.02 test F1. They do not refute the explanation. The label matches the predicate, and every variable in the predicate is observable at D2.
